lesson.title: The major fields of psychology
lesson.summary: Psychology includes fields that differ in their questions, levels of analysis and settings of application. This lesson shows how several perspectives can be relevant to the same phenomenon without reducing the discipline to clinical psychology or forcing every situation into a single field.
objectives: Identify the characteristic questions of several major fields of psychology.
Distinguish a field of research, a level of explanation and a professional setting.
Use biological, cognitive, developmental and social perspectives to analyse the same situation.
Distinguish the production of fundamental knowledge from the application of psychological knowledge.
prerequisites: Define psychology as the scientific study of behaviour and mental processes.
Distinguish observable behaviour, mental processes and indicators.

content.text: Psychology is not a single, uniform field. Its areas develop around different questions, populations, levels of analysis and settings. Cognitive psychology studies attention, memory, language and reasoning; developmental psychology examines change across the lifespan; social psychology investigates the influence of other people and groups; and biopsychology connects biological functioning with behaviour. This map is useful, but it is neither exhaustive nor made of rigid boundaries.

A field is a set of questions and methods, whereas a level of explanation describes the angle from which a phenomenon is studied. To explain difficulty concentrating, researchers might examine sleep and biological functioning, attentional mechanisms, developmental change or the influence of the social environment. These explanations may complement one another when they concern distinct mechanisms.

Invented example: a student repeatedly postpones her work. A cognitive approach might examine working memory and attentional control; a developmental approach, the development of self-regulation; a social approach, group norms and comparison with peers; and a health approach, sleep and stress. Naming several fields does not remove the need to formulate testable hypotheses and collect evidence.

The distinction between fundamental research and application concerns the immediate purpose of the work, not a hierarchy of value. Fundamental research primarily seeks to understand a mechanism. Applied work uses or evaluates knowledge in health, education, employment, justice or other settings. The same field can combine research and practice: clinical, occupational and health psychology also produce knowledge, while cognitive or social findings can guide interventions.

Common misconception: psychology and psychotherapy are not the same thing. Clinical psychology is important, but the discipline also studies the brain and behaviour, perception, learning, development, personality, social relationships, health, education, work and many other topics. To place a question, first ask what phenomenon is being studied, at what level, and for what purpose.

concepts.title: Diversity of psychological fields
concepts.description: Fields of psychology differ in questions, methods, populations and settings, and their boundaries often overlap.

concepts.title: Complementary levels of explanation
concepts.description: The same behaviour can be studied at biological, cognitive, developmental and social levels that answer different questions.

concepts.title: Research and applications
concepts.description: Research produces knowledge, while applications use or evaluate knowledge in a setting; one field may perform both functions.

tasks.title: Map the fields
tasks.description: After reading OpenStax, produce a table of eight fields with a typical question, a main level of analysis and an application for each. Identify two overlaps between fields.

tasks.title: Place six questions
tasks.description: Assign six supplied or invented questions to one or more fields. Justify each choice using the object of study rather than a keyword, and accept more than one field when the questions differ.

tasks.title: Build a multilevel analysis
tasks.description: Choose an everyday situation and formulate four distinct questions: biological, cognitive, developmental and social. Propose one observable measure for each.

editorial.audience: Adult beginners with no university prerequisites

questions.prompt: Which field primarily studies psychological change across the lifespan?
questions.explanation: Developmental psychology studies change and continuity at different ages.

questions.prompt: Which question most directly belongs to cognitive psychology?
questions.explanation: Cognitive psychology studies attention, memory, language and reasoning.

options.label: How does attention affect recall of a word list?
How should a team schedule be organised?
How does average population height change?
Which law regulates a professional title?

questions.prompt: Which statements about fields of psychology are accurate?
questions.explanation: Fields can overlap and differ in their questions, methods or settings; an introductory list is not exhaustive.

options.label: They can differ in questions and methods.
Every situation belongs to exactly one field.
A list of fields is always final.

questions.prompt: Clinical psychology represents the whole of psychology.
questions.explanation: Clinical psychology is one field among many fundamental and applied areas.

questions.prompt: What is the best criterion for placing a new question within a field?
questions.explanation: Start with the phenomenon, question and level of analysis rather than a keyword.

options.label: The precise object and research question

questions.prompt: Which question mainly uses a social level of explanation?
questions.explanation: The effect of group norms on behaviour is a social-psychological question.

options.label: How do group norms influence risk-taking?
How does the ability change between ages 6 and 12?

questions.prompt: Which question mainly uses a biological level of explanation?
questions.explanation: Measures of neural or physiological mechanisms mainly concern a biological level.

options.label: Which brain networks are active during the task?
Which expectations does the group communicate?
How does this ability change with age?

questions.prompt: Why can several levels of explanation be relevant to one behaviour?
questions.explanation: They can address different mechanisms and support complementary hypotheses, all of which still require evidence.

options.label: They prove that evidence is unnecessary.
They guarantee that every explanation is true.

questions.prompt: A brain-based explanation automatically makes cognitive or social explanations unnecessary.
questions.explanation: Different levels may answer different questions and can complement one another.

questions.prompt: After proposing four levels of explanation for procrastination, what comes next scientifically?
questions.explanation: The perspectives must become testable hypotheses linked to relevant evidence.

options.label: Formulate testable hypotheses and define the required evidence
Choose the explanation that feels most intuitive

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes fundamental research?
questions.explanation: Its immediate purpose is to understand a mechanism or pattern, even if applications may follow.

options.label: Studying how attention selects competing information
Choosing a slogan without evaluating it

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes applied work?
questions.explanation: Applied work uses or evaluates knowledge in a concrete setting.

options.label: Evaluating a workplace change intended to reduce errors
Only describing the history of a concept

questions.prompt: Which statements about research and application are correct?
questions.explanation: A field may create and apply knowledge, and applications can be evaluated empirically.

options.label: One field can combine research and practice.
An application can be evaluated scientifically.
Fundamental research can never become useful.

questions.prompt: “Applied” means that scientific methods are no longer necessary.
questions.explanation: Applications also need clear objectives, outcome measures and acknowledged limits.

questions.prompt: An occupational psychologist tests whether a new organisation reduces errors. Which description is most accurate?
questions.explanation: Applied work and empirical evaluation can occur together.

options.label: Application and empirical evaluation can be combined.
It cannot be psychology because it occurs at work.
